name: Novocomum
features: Five-storey apartment block whose cut-away corners hold glazed cylinders, nicknamed the 'Transatlantico'.
note: Terragni died in 1943, so his buildings are public domain in Italy and Commons keeps photos.

name: Casa Rustici
features: Two parallel slabs tied across the street front by thin balcony frames, leaving an open court between.
note: Only 1024px photos; usable under the 800px rule. Check that 'Category:Casa Comolli-Rustici' (also by Terragni and Lingeri) is a different building before mixing files.

name: Stadio Artemio Franchi
features: Cantilevered concrete canopy over the main stand, helical ramps and the slender Marathon Tower.

photos.file: File:Firenze, stadio artemio franchi, tribuna centrale con copertura sospesa originale 00.jpg
File:Firenze, stadio artemio franchi, scala elicoidale 01.jpg
File:Firenze, stadio artemio franchi, torre di maratona 01.jpg
File:Firenze, stadio artemio franchi, sostegni delle tribune 01.jpg

note: Plenty of CC BY 3.0 photos of Nervi's canopy, stairs and tower.

name: Palazzo dei Congressi
features: Granite-columned portico before a cubic hall roofed by a cross vault; roof terrace with open-air theatre.

photos.file: File:Palazzo dei Congressi a EUR Roma.jpg

note: Designed 1937-38, completed after the war (1954). Many free photos.

name: Villa Girasole
features: An L-shaped house that turns on a circular base to follow the sun, round a central tower.

photos.file: File:Veduta di Villa Girasole, Marcellise, Verona (1936).jpg

note: Only two files; check the panorama shows the house clearly.

name: Mausoleo delle Fosse Ardeatine
by: Mario Fiorentino, Giuseppe Perugini, Nello Aprile, Cino Calcaprina, Aldo Cardelli
features: A single huge concrete slab hovers low over the rows of tombs, lit by a thin band of light at its edge.
commons_category: Category:Monument to the victims of the Ardeatine massacre

photos.file: File:Entrance gate at the Mausoleo delle Fosse Ardeatine.jpg

name: Teatro del Mondo
features: A floating timber theatre: a square box, an octagonal drum and a pointed roof, towed on a barge.
note: Built for the 1979-80 Venice Biennale and dismantled in 1981. Check the photos are of the original (not a model or the 2004 Genoa reconstruction) and are the uploader's own work.

name: Casa alle Zattere
features: A modern house on the Giudecca canal that reworks the Venetian palazzo: plaster walls, framed windows.
note: Also a 1982 Paolo Monti photo (BEIC, CC BY-SA 4.0, 1280px).

name: Chiesa Madre di Gibellina
features: A great white sphere set on a cubic block, built in the new town after the 1968 Belice earthquake.
note: Designed 1972, roof collapsed during construction; completed about 2010. Year is completion; verify against a source before publishing.

name: Santa Maria Assunta, Riola
features: Stepped roof over curved concrete arches pours light into the nave; a separate open bell frame stands beside it.

photos.file: File:Vergato - Chiesa di Santa Maria Assunta - 2023-09-26 10-59-43 001.jpg

note: Aalto's only building in Italy; completed after his death (1976).

name: Teatro Regio
features: Mollino's brick-walled opera house behind the old 18th-century facade, with a shell-shaped hall inside.
note: Check which exterior photos show Mollino's 1973 building rather than only the old Piazza Castello front.

name: La Rinascente, Piazza Fiume
features: Department store with an exposed steel frame and red-granite panels that hide ducts in their ribbed folds.

photos.file: File:Edificio che ospita la Rinascente di piazza Fiume a Roma.jpg

note: 'Workplace' is the nearest type for a department store.

name: Ponte Musmeci (Viadotto dell'Industria)
features: A continuous thin concrete membrane, form-found from soap-film models, carries the deck over four spans.

photos.file: File:Ponte sul Basento, opera di Sergio Musmeci 2.jpg

name: Corviale
features: A single housing slab nearly a kilometre long on the edge of Rome, with a fourth-floor street meant for shops.

name: Vele di Scampia
features: Sail-shaped housing blocks: two stepped slabs leaning together around a tall internal street of walkways.
note: Several of the seven Vele have been demolished since 2020; completion year approximate (built 1962-75).

name: La Nuvola (Roma Convention Center)
features: A glass-and-steel box holds 'the Cloud', a free-form fabric-skinned auditorium hanging inside it.

photos.file: File:Interior of New Congress Center "La Nuvola" in Rome.jpg

note: 'Fuksas Cloud.jpg' is marked public domain; check the claim before use.

name: Genova San Giorgio Bridge
features: A steel deck shaped like a ship's hull on elliptical concrete piers, replacing the collapsed Morandi bridge.

photos.file: File:Ponte San Giorgio, Genova, sul torrente Valpolcevera.jpg

note: Steel is the main material; 'Steel & glass' is the nearest concept.

name: Museo Enzo Ferrari
features: A yellow aluminium roof, shaped like a car bonnet with air-intake slots, curls round Enzo Ferrari's birthplace.

photos.file: File:Direction of Museo Casa Enzo Ferrari in 2018.01.jpg
File:Direction of Museo Casa Enzo Ferrari in 2018.02.jpg

note: 14 photos in the 2018 series; pick ones that show the roof.

name: Fondazione Giangiacomo Feltrinelli
features: A long, thin glass-and-concrete gabled building whose steep roof repeats the rhythm of its frame.
note: One 1647px photo; more may exist under Porta Volta categories.

name: Talponia (Unità residenziale Ovest)
features: Olivetti staff housing buried in a hill: a curved glass front under a grassed roof walkway.

photos.file: File:Ivrea. Facciata vetrata dell'unità residenziale Ovest Olivetti Talponia.jpg
File:Ivrea. Unità residenziale Ovest Olivetti Talponia vista dal tetto.jpg

note: No dedicated category ('Category:Talponia' is a moth genus).

name: Collegio del Colle
features: Student rooms in brick-and-concrete terraces that step down the hillside facing Urbino.
note: 'Collegi urbino.jpg' (5801px) may show the wider campus; the TIFFs are 1614px.

name: Villa La Saracena
features: Seaside villa of white walls and a long curving wall that leads to a shell-like hall opening to the sea.
note: Only one photo (Paolo Monti, 1280px); check it shows the exterior.

name: Banca Popolare di Verona
features: Stone facade on Piazza Nogara pierced by scattered round windows, topped by a loggia under a thin roof.
note: Only a 900px photo (described as the bank's main headquarters on Piazza Nogara), usable under the 800px rule; the larger Piazza Nogara photos may also show it. Finished by Arrigo Rudi after Scarpa's death (1978).

name: Ceramica Artistica Solimene
features: A ceramics factory whose facade is a wall of clay pots set in tapering cones, wrapped round a spiral ramp.
note: Completion year approximate (1951-55); check before publishing.

name: Olivetti Factory, Pozzuoli
features: A humane factory laid out in low wings and gardens facing the Gulf of Pozzuoli.
note: Two Paolo Monti photos (1280px and 1043px); check they show the exterior.

name: Santa Maria Immacolata, Longarone
features: Rebuilt after the 1963 Vajont flood: a concrete church whose roof is a curved open-air amphitheatre.

photos.file: File:Longarone (BL) - chiesa di Santa Maria Immacolata.jpg

note: Rebuilt after the 1963 Vajont disaster; completion year approximate (1975-83).

name: Xenia Hotel, Mykonos
features: Low whitewashed volumes and stone walls step with the ground, reading the Cycladic village in a modern frame.
note: One 1970 photo; year of completion approximate.

name: Archaeological Museum of Ioannina
features: Concrete frame filled with local stone, low pavilions round a courtyard in a park.
note: Most files are of exhibits; one 2527px entrance photo plus a 960px view ('Archaeological Museum of Ioannina.jpg'). Some of the '2024' series may also show the building.

name: Athens Conservatoire
features: A long grid-framed concrete block over an open ground floor, part of an unfinished cultural centre.

photos.file: File:The facade of the Athens Conservatoire.jpg
File:The exterior of the Athens Conservatoire.jpg
File:The facade of the Athens Conservatoire (5).jpg

note: Designed 1959, built 1969-76.

name: Hilton Athens
by: Prokopis Vassiliadis, Emmanouil Vourekas, Spyros Staikos
features: A gently bent white slab with engraved marble end walls, the first big International Style hotel in Athens.

photos.file: File:The Athens Hilton as seen from the neighbourhood of Pagrati.jpg

name: Museum of Byzantine Culture
features: Brick-faced volumes and deep slots of light lead visitors on a slow route through the collection.
commons_category: Category:Exterior of Museum of Byzantine Culture

photos.file: File:Museum of Byzantine Culture, Thessaloniki, Greece (9168128342).jpg
File:Museum of Byzantine Culture, Thessaloniki, Greece (9182809550).jpg

name: Blue Building (Blue Condominium)
features: Interwar apartment block on Exarchia Square, its corner wrapped in curved cantilevered balconies.
note: Only one file found; no category.

name: Lycabettus Theatre
features: An open-air theatre in an old quarry on Lycabettus hill, its seating built as a light, demountable steel frame.

photos.file: File:The Theatre of Lycabettus on November 30, 2019.jpg

note: Zenetos's original 1965 seating has since been rebuilt; check what the photos show.

name: Renzo Piano Building Workshop, Punta Nave
features: Piano's own studio: glass roofs stepping down terraces to the sea, reached by a small funicular.

photos.file: File:Particolare del Renzo Piano Building Workshop a Genova Vesima (Punta Nave), luglio 2013.jpg

note: Only an 809px detail photo; usable under the 800px rule if it clearly shows the building. If not, this is a good candidate to draw (stepped glass roofs down the hillside).

name: Casa del Girasole
features: A rusticated stone base and a front split down the middle under a broken gable: modernism playing with the classical.

photos.file: File:Paolo Monti - Servizio fotografico - BEIC 6356070 sw.jpg

note: Only Paolo Monti's 1951 photo (1242px), filed under Viale Bruno Buozzi / Luigi Moretti / built 1950 but not named; it should be the Girasole (Viale Bruno Buozzi 64). Check before use.

name: Elementary School, Fagnano Olona
features: Classrooms round a courtyard with a cylindrical library, a chimney and a stepped stair like a small theatre.
note: No dedicated category; files sit directly in Category:Aldo Rossi.

name: Casa Papanice
features: Curving walls and a ribbed facade of coloured ceramic-tube 'organ pipes' spread out from the corners.
note: Most of the category is film stills; one 5589px building photo.

name: Cartiera Burgo
features: A 250 m paper-mill roof hung like a suspension bridge from chains over two 50 m concrete trestles.
view: long side elevation: the 250 m hall with the two concrete trestles 43 m in from each end, the chains sagging between them and running down to the cantilevered roof ends, with vertical hangers
note: No photo of the Mantua mill on Commons (Category:Cartiere Burgo holds only other Burgo plants). Sources (via search summaries) give 250 m length, 160-164 m clear span with ~43 m cantilevers each end, trestles 47-50 m high, roof about 22 m up; proportions drawn to those. Each trestle is a coupled pair of pylons straddling the hall, so it reads as a single tapered pylon in side view. Nervi worked with Gino Covre.

name: Weekend House, Anavyssos
features: Thick local-stone piers carry a flat concrete slab, making a shaded portico that wraps two sides of a small house.
view: elevation of the portico side: the thin flat concrete roof slab on rectangular stone piers, the house sitting on a low platform
note: No Commons photo. Sources: square/rectangular plan on a 2x5 m grid, an L-shaped portico 2-3 m deep on two sides, flat exposed-concrete slab on six rectangular stone pillars, load-bearing stone walls. The number and spacing of piers shown on this one side (four) is my reading of the six-pillar L; check against the published plan.

name: Lanaras Weekend House
features: Two thin concrete slabs on slender steel posts, glazed and shuttered between, above stone terrace walls.
view: long elevation toward the sea: thin floor and roof slabs projecting past the glass line, slender steel posts with glazing and a shutter rail between, a stone base and stone terrace walls of different heights either side
note: No Commons photo. Sources: two thin reinforced-concrete slabs with slim projections on thin metal supports, sides filled with glass and sliding shutters, stone retaining walls of different heights, bedroom wing at right angles (not shown). Bay count is indicative, not counted from a plan.

name: Onassis Stegi
features: A box wrapped on all four sides in thin horizontal bands of white marble that glow from inside at night.
view: front elevation on Syngrou Avenue: the marble-banded box over a glazed ground floor
note: Commons has only interior photos. Sources: white marble strips wrap all four facades; building about 27 m (89 ft) tall. The width-to-height ratio and band spacing are approximate.

name: Circular School, Agios Dimitrios
features: A three-storey disc of classrooms round a central core, its south half ringed by louvred eaves at every floor.
view: slightly raised view from the south: the three-storey drum with a louvred eave band at each floor head round the southern half, and glazed walls with metal mullions
note: No Commons photo. Sources: three-floor circular building, three standard modules of 160 pupils per floor round a central audio-visual core, concrete and metal, 'a succession of louvred roofs surrounding the southern semi-circle of the three floors'. Diameter-to-height ratio and mullion count are approximate. Built 1970-76 (designed 1969); Agios Dimitrios is a suburb of Athens, not Lycabettus.

name: Casa Baldi
features: Load-bearing tufa walls curve concave outside and convex inside, a Borromini-inspired modern house on a quarried hill.
note: No Commons photo (Category:Casa Baldi (Olevano Romano) is a different building). Sources confirm curved tufa walls and a flat roof, and a level added in 1971, but the arrangement of walls and roof planes can't be fixed from text alone; an elevation would also hide the curves. Needs a plan or photo to draw.

name: Casa Giuliani-Frigerio
features: Every facade is composed differently, balcony planes projecting before recessed windows; Terragni's last building.
note: No Commons photo found, though Terragni died in 1943 so photos would be free in Italy; worth asking for an upload. Sources disagree on storey count (four vs five) and the four facades differ in detail, so I didn't draw it.

name: Zanussi Offices
features: Exposed-concrete offices forming the factory's edge on the main road, with sloping glass terraces lit from above.
note: No Commons photo. Sources give exposed concrete, a long edge along via Pontebbana and sloping glass terraces on the north side, but not enough to fix the section and facade with confidence.

name: Villa Ottolenghi
features: A house sunk into the slope above Lake Garda, its walkable roof level with the road, on nine drum columns.
note: No Commons photo. Mostly buried in the hillside, so an elevation would show little; the U-shaped plan and column layout would need the published drawings. Designed 1974, finished after Scarpa's death (1978).
